8: ---
9: 
10: # create-diff
11: 
12: > Capture what changed in an edited document, offline, without Git, as one HTML report you can open in any browser.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
17: 
18: | Aspect | What you get |
19: |---|---|
20: | **Use it for** | Reviewing what changed in a locally edited Markdown, text, HTML, DOCX or text-PDF document without Git |
21: | **Invoke with** | `python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot / compare / compare-pair` or `/create:diff` |
22: | **Works on** | One document at a time or a pre-composed multi-file aggregate pair |
23: | **Produces** | A single self-contained HTML report with inlined CSS, zero JavaScript, no remote references and no network calls |
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. OVERVIEW
28: 
29: ### Why This Skill Exists
30: 
31: Not everything you edit lives in Git. An AI or a person edits a Markdown spec, a DOCX brief, a PDF export or a text file outside version control and now needs to know exactly what changed before trusting it. Diffing that by eye is unreliable beyond a sentence. Pasting the file into a hosted diff tool sends its content somewhere you may not want it to go. create-diff exists so review works the same everywhere: local and offline, never touching the source file.
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: create-diff captures a baseline snapshot of a document before an edit happens, then compares the current file against that snapshot or an explicit second file and renders one self-contained HTML report you can open offline. The engine ships as `scripts/create_diff.py` and reads Markdown, plain text, HTML, DOCX and text-layer PDF. It does not touch code or Git-tracked files: that boundary belongs to `sk-git`. It does not audit a single document on its own either, since comparing two states is the point. `create-quality-control` handles single-document scoring.
36: 
37: ### When To Use This Skill
38: 
39: Use create-diff when:
40: 
41: - An AI or a person edited a document outside Git and you need proof of what changed.
42: - You want a baseline captured before a risky edit.
43: - A pre-composed multi-file bundle needs its transitions to stay visible in review.
44: 
45: Skip it when:
46: 
47: - The files are code or already tracked in Git (`sk-git` owns that).
48: - The comparison is visual or pixel-level (out of scope: create-diff compares extracted text only).
49: - You are scoring a single document with no second state to compare (`create-quality-control` owns that).
50: 
51: ### The Format Fidelity Layer
52: 
53: Every comparison runs at a stated fidelity tier so a limited result is never mistaken for a complete one. The engine extracts what a format can honestly give:
54: 
55: | Format | What the skill knows how to operate |
56: |---|---|
57: | **Plain text** | diff `.txt`, `.log`, `.csv` and unknown text-like files at full fidelity after normalization |
58: | **Markdown** | diff `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mdown` files at full fidelity, comparing normalized text with rendered HTML left out |
59: | **HTML** | extract visible text and `h1` to `h6` headings at text fidelity, with CSS and scripts left out |
60: | **DOCX** | compare paragraph text, table text and heading-styled paragraphs at text fidelity |
61: | **PDF** | diff the extracted text layer at `text*` fidelity when a local extractor is installed, with scanned pages warned and OCR out of scope |
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. QUICK START
66: 
67: **Step 1: capture a baseline before the edit.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
71: ```
72: 
73: Confirms a snapshot was stored. Nothing else changes.
74: 
75: **Step 2: after the edit, compare and render.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
79: ```
80: 
81: Or, without a stored baseline, compare two explicit files directly using the shipped fixtures:
82: 
83: ```bash
84: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair \
85:   --before assets/fixtures/onboarding-before.md \
86:   --after  assets/fixtures/onboarding-after.md \
87:   --report /tmp/onboarding-review.html
88: ```
89: 
90: You get one HTML file with a change summary line like `markdown, tier full, +6 -0 ~3` and a unified or side-by-side diff view.
91: 
92: **Step 3: verify the report before you hand it off.**
93: 
94: ```bash
95: python3 scripts/validate_report.py /tmp/onboarding-review.html
96: ```
97: 
98: Prints `PASS` when the report is safe and self-contained.
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
103: 
104: The lifecycle has one hard invariant: the baseline has to exist before the edit happens.
105: 
106: - `snapshot` copies the current file into a local `.create-diff/` store without altering the source.
107: - Once the edit is done, `compare` diffs the live file against its latest stored baseline and writes the report.
108: - When no baseline exists or you already have two explicit versions, `compare-pair` skips the store entirely and diffs `--before` against `--after`.
109: - Either path ends the same way: a deterministic line-and-word diff, run through a format-aware extractor and rendered into one inlined-CSS HTML file with no scripts and no network calls.
110: 
111: ### Key Concept: Aggregate File Boundaries
112: 
113: `compare-pair` can also review a bundle of files in one call, as long as both `--before` and `--after` wrap every file in matching `===== BEGIN FILE: <path> =====` and `===== END FILE: <path> =====` markers. When the markers line up, the report renders each transition as a full-width boundary band with a canvas gap before it, so a five-file bundle still reads as five distinct reviews instead of one file's heading bleeding into the next. Malformed or unbalanced markers just render as ordinary text. The CLI itself still only ever receives one before-document and one after-document.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
118: 
119: ### Related Skills
120: 
121: | Skill | Relationship |
122: |---|---|
123: | `sk-git` | Owns diffs for code and Git-tracked files. create-diff is for everything outside that boundary. |
124: | Visual / pixel-level comparison | Out of scope: create-diff only compares extracted text. |
125: | `create-quality-control` | Audits one existing document. create-diff always compares two states. |
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
130: 
131: | What you see | Why | Fix |
132: |---|---|---|
133: | Exit `4`, missing baseline | `compare` ran with no stored snapshot for that file | Run `snapshot` first or use `compare-pair` with explicit `--before` and `--after` |
134: | Exit `3`, unsupported format | The file type has no extractor or the PDF has no text layer | Run `capabilities` to see what is available or provide a pre-extracted explicit pair |
135: | Report already exists | The engine refuses to overwrite an existing report path | Pass a new `--report` path or remove the old file first |
136: | File-boundary bands missing on a multi-file pair | The `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers are unbalanced or unmatched between the two inputs | Match marker order and paths exactly in both `--before` and `--after` |
137: | `validate_report.py` fails | The report references a remote resource or an inline script somehow made it through | Fix the renderer input and regenerate. Never hand off a failed report as clean |
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## 7. FAQ
142: 
143: **Q: Why not just use `git diff` for this?**
144: 
145: A: Git needs the file under version control with commit history. create-diff works on any document, anywhere on disk, without ever needing a Git repo.
146: 
147: **Q: Does this send my document anywhere?**
148: 
149: A: No. Everything runs locally with the Python standard library. The report has no scripts and no remote references. When PDF extraction is available it uses a local extractor only.
150: 
151: **Q: What if the document is a scanned PDF?**
152: 
153: A: There is no text layer to diff, so the comparison would be empty. OCR is out of scope. Use the explicit-pair fallback with pre-extracted text instead.
154: 
155: **Q: Can I compare more than two files at once?**
156: 
157: A: `compare-pair` accepts one before-document and one after-document, but you can pre-compose either side into a multi-file bundle using the `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers described in Section 4.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 8. VERIFICATION
162: 
163: | Check | Result |
164: |---|---|
165: | `python3 scripts/validate_report.py <report>` | `PASS` (asserts doctype, `lang`, a CSP meta tag, zero `<script>`, no inline handlers and no remote resources) |
166: | Source unchanged | The source file stays byte-for-byte identical before and after `compare` or `compare-pair` |
167: | Manual scenarios | `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` groups scenarios by snapshot lifecycle, comparison formats and safety guarantees |
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 9. RELATED DOCUMENTS
172: 
173: | Document | Purpose |
174: |---|---|
175: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Authoritative packet contract and rules |
176: | [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) | Machine router: intent map, resource map and loading levels |

8: ---
9: 
10: # create-diff
11: 
12: > Capture what changed in an edited document, offline, without Git, as one HTML report you can open in any browser.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
17: 
18: | Aspect | What you get |
19: |---|---|
20: | **Use it for** | Reviewing what changed in a locally edited Markdown, text, HTML, DOCX or text-PDF document without Git |
21: | **Invoke with** | `python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot / compare / compare-pair` or `/create:diff` |
22: | **Works on** | One document at a time or a pre-composed multi-file aggregate pair |
23: | **Produces** | A single self-contained HTML report with inlined CSS, zero JavaScript, no remote references and no network calls |
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. OVERVIEW
28: 
29: ### Why This Skill Exists
30: 
31: Not everything you edit lives in Git. An AI or a person edits a Markdown spec, a DOCX brief, a PDF export or a text file outside version control and now needs to know exactly what changed before trusting it. Diffing that by eye is unreliable beyond a sentence. Pasting the file into a hosted diff tool sends its content somewhere you may not want it to go. create-diff exists so review works the same everywhere: local and offline, never touching the source file.
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: create-diff captures a baseline snapshot of a document before an edit happens, then compares the current file against that snapshot or an explicit second file and renders one self-contained HTML report you can open offline. The engine ships as `scripts/create_diff.py` and reads Markdown, plain text, HTML, DOCX and text-layer PDF. It does not touch code or Git-tracked files: that boundary belongs to `sk-git`. It does not audit a single document on its own either, since comparing two states is the point. `create-quality-control` handles single-document scoring.
36: 
37: ### When To Use This Skill
38: 
39: Use create-diff when:
40: 
41: - An AI or a person edited a document outside Git and you need proof of what changed.
42: - You want a baseline captured before a risky edit.
43: - A pre-composed multi-file bundle needs its transitions to stay visible in review.
44: 
45: Skip it when:
46: 
47: - The files are code or already tracked in Git (`sk-git` owns that).
48: - The comparison is visual or pixel-level (out of scope: create-diff compares extracted text only).
49: - You are scoring a single document with no second state to compare (`create-quality-control` owns that).
50: 
51: ### The Format Fidelity Layer
52: 
53: Every comparison runs at a stated fidelity tier so a limited result is never mistaken for a complete one. The engine extracts what a format can honestly give:
54: 
55: | Format | What the skill knows how to operate |
56: |---|---|
57: | **Plain text** | diff `.txt`, `.log`, `.csv` and unknown text-like files at full fidelity after normalization |
58: | **Markdown** | diff `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mdown` files at full fidelity, comparing normalized text with rendered HTML left out |
59: | **HTML** | extract visible text and `h1` to `h6` headings at text fidelity, with CSS and scripts left out |
60: | **DOCX** | compare paragraph text, table text and heading-styled paragraphs at text fidelity |
61: | **PDF** | diff the extracted text layer at `text*` fidelity when a local extractor is installed, with scanned pages warned and OCR out of scope |
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. QUICK START
66: 
67: **Step 1: capture a baseline before the edit.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
71: ```
72: 
73: Confirms a snapshot was stored. Nothing else changes.
74: 
75: **Step 2: after the edit, compare and render.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
79: ```
80: 
81: Or, without a stored baseline, compare two explicit files directly using the shipped fixtures:
82: 
83: ```bash
84: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair \
85:   --before assets/fixtures/onboarding-before.md \
86:   --after  assets/fixtures/onboarding-after.md \
87:   --report /tmp/onboarding-review.html
88: ```
89: 
90: You get one HTML file with a change summary line like `markdown, tier full, +6 -0 ~3` and a unified or side-by-side diff view.
91: 
92: **Step 3: verify the report before you hand it off.**
93: 
94: ```bash
95: python3 scripts/validate_report.py /tmp/onboarding-review.html
96: ```
97: 
98: Prints `PASS` when the report is safe and self-contained.
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
103: 
104: The lifecycle has one hard invariant: the baseline has to exist before the edit happens.
105: 
106: - `snapshot` copies the current file into a local `.create-diff/` store without altering the source.
107: - Once the edit is done, `compare` diffs the live file against its latest stored baseline and writes the report.
108: - When no baseline exists or you already have two explicit versions, `compare-pair` skips the store entirely and diffs `--before` against `--after`.
109: - Either path ends the same way: a deterministic line-and-word diff, run through a format-aware extractor and rendered into one inlined-CSS HTML file with no scripts and no network calls.
110: 
111: ### Key Concept: Aggregate File Boundaries
112: 
113: `compare-pair` can also review a bundle of files in one call, as long as both `--before` and `--after` wrap every file in matching `===== BEGIN FILE: <path> =====` and `===== END FILE: <path> =====` markers. When the markers line up, the report renders each transition as a full-width boundary band with a canvas gap before it, so a five-file bundle still reads as five distinct reviews instead of one file's heading bleeding into the next. Malformed or unbalanced markers just render as ordinary text. The CLI itself still only ever receives one before-document and one after-document.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
118: 
119: ### Related Skills
120: 
121: | Skill | Relationship |
122: |---|---|
123: | `sk-git` | Owns diffs for code and Git-tracked files. create-diff is for everything outside that boundary. |
124: | Visual / pixel-level comparison | Out of scope: create-diff only compares extracted text. |
125: | `create-quality-control` | Audits one existing document. create-diff always compares two states. |
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
130: 
131: | What you see | Why | Fix |
132: |---|---|---|
133: | Exit `4`, missing baseline | `compare` ran with no stored snapshot for that file | Run `snapshot` first or use `compare-pair` with explicit `--before` and `--after` |
134: | Exit `3`, unsupported format | The file type has no extractor or the PDF has no text layer | Run `capabilities` to see what is available or provide a pre-extracted explicit pair |
135: | Report already exists | The engine refuses to overwrite an existing report path | Pass a new `--report` path or remove the old file first |
136: | File-boundary bands missing on a multi-file pair | The `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers are unbalanced or unmatched between the two inputs | Match marker order and paths exactly in both `--before` and `--after` |
137: | `validate_report.py` fails | The report references a remote resource or an inline script somehow made it through | Fix the renderer input and regenerate. Never hand off a failed report as clean |
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## 7. FAQ
142: 
143: **Q: Why not just use `git diff` for this?**
144: 
145: A: Git needs the file under version control with commit history. create-diff works on any document, anywhere on disk, without ever needing a Git repo.
146: 
147: **Q: Does this send my document anywhere?**
148: 
149: A: No. Everything runs locally with the Python standard library. The report has no scripts and no remote references. When PDF extraction is available it uses a local extractor only.
150: 
151: **Q: What if the document is a scanned PDF?**
152: 
153: A: There is no text layer to diff, so the comparison would be empty. OCR is out of scope. Use the explicit-pair fallback with pre-extracted text instead.
154: 
155: **Q: Can I compare more than two files at once?**
156: 
157: A: `compare-pair` accepts one before-document and one after-document, but you can pre-compose either side into a multi-file bundle using the `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers described in Section 4.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 8. VERIFICATION
162: 
163: | Check | Result |
164: |---|---|
165: | `python3 scripts/validate_report.py <report>` | `PASS` (asserts doctype, `lang`, a CSP meta tag, zero `<script>`, no inline handlers and no remote resources) |
166: | Source unchanged | The source file stays byte-for-byte identical before and after `compare` or `compare-pair` |
167: | Manual scenarios | `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` groups scenarios by snapshot lifecycle, comparison formats and safety guarantees |
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 9. RELATED DOCUMENTS
172: 
173: | Document | Purpose |
174: |---|---|
175: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Authoritative packet contract and rules |
176: | [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) | Machine router: intent map, resource map and loading levels |
177: | [`references/README.md`](./references/README.md) | Reference route-map |
178: | [`references/cli-reference.md`](./references/cli-reference.md) | Full command, flag and exit-code reference |
179: | [`references/capabilities-and-fidelity.md`](./references/capabilities-and-fidelity.md) | Format support matrix and fidelity tiers |
180: | [`references/workflow.md`](./references/workflow.md) | Baseline, explicit-pair and snapshot lifecycle |
181: | [`references/accessibility-contract.md`](./references/accessibility-contract.md) | The report's accessibility guarantees |
182: | [`references/worked-example.md`](./references/worked-example.md) | End-to-end walkthrough using the shipped fixtures |
183: | [`assets/fixtures/README.md`](./assets/fixtures/README.md) | Runnable before/after worked example |
184: | [`feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`](./feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md) | Canonical capability inventory |

64: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
65: 
66: All comparison, extraction, snapshotting, and rendering are done by `scripts/create_diff.py`. Run it from this packet directory (or give an absolute path to it). The invariant is: **capture the baseline before the edit** — a diff needs a real before-state.

68: ### Automatic flow (snapshot-backed)
69: 
70: ```bash
71: # 0. (optional) confirm what is supported and at what fidelity
72: python3 scripts/create_diff.py capabilities
73: 
74: # 1. BEFORE the edit — capture a baseline (copies the file into a local .create-diff/ store;
75: #    never touches the source)
76: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
77: 
78: # 2. ... let the edit happen (AI or human) ...
79: 
80: # 3. AFTER the edit — compare the current file against its latest baseline and render the report
81: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Explicit-pair flow (fallback — no stored state needed)
85: 
86: Use this when there is no baseline, when comparing two arbitrary versions, or when the automatic store is unavailable:
87: 
88: ```bash
89: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair --before old.md --after new.md --report review.html
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Pre-composed aggregate pairs
93: 
94: `compare-pair` can also review a pre-composed pair containing two or more files.
95: Wrap every file in both inputs with the same ordered, unique markers:
96: 
97: ```text
98: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/first.md =====
99: [file content]
100: ===== END FILE: docs/first.md =====
101: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/second.md =====
102: [file content]
103: ===== END FILE: docs/second.md =====
104: ```
105: 
106: When both inputs contain a balanced matching envelope, the report renders every
107: start and end as an explicit full-width boundary band. Boundaries stay visible
108: through collapsed context, later files receive a 32px canvas gap before their
109: start band, and transitions reset Markdown section labels between files. This
110: does not add native directory comparison or repeated multi-file CLI arguments;
111: callers compose the two aggregate documents before invoking `compare-pair`.
112: 
113: ### Report and verification
114: 
115: - The report is a single self-contained HTML file (inlined CSS, no scripts, no network). Views: `--view unified` (default) or `--view side-by-side`.
116: - Valid aggregate pairs display semantic `START FILE` and `END FILE` bands in both views; malformed envelopes remain ordinary document text.
117: - Without `--report`, the source stem is semantically normalized to lowercase kebab-case and emitted as `<source-slug>.diff.html`. An explicit report basename must already use lowercase kebab-case and the engine refuses to overwrite an existing report.
118: - Always verify a generated report is safe and self-contained before handing it off:
119: 
120: ```bash
121: python3 scripts/validate_report.py review.html
122: ```
123: 
124: ### Lifecycle helpers
125: 
126: ```bash
127: python3 scripts/create_diff.py status [path/to/doc.md]      # list stored baselines
128: python3 scripts/create_diff.py cleanup --older-than 14      # prune old baselines (add --dry-run to preview)
129: ```
130: 
131: ### Machine-readable output and exit codes
132: 
133: Add `--json` to `compare`, `compare-pair`, `capabilities`, or `status` for a structured summary. Exit codes: `0` success · `2` usage error · `3` unsupported/limited format with no fallback · `4` missing baseline snapshot · `5` I/O or extraction failure. Map these to actionable messages rather than swallowing them.
134:

136: 
137: ## 4. CAPABILITY & FIDELITY TIERS
138: 
139: State the tier to the user; never present a low-fidelity comparison as complete.
140: 
141: | Format | Tier | What is compared | Not compared |
142: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
143: | text | full | exact text | — |
144: | markdown | full | exact text + heading/section awareness | rendered-HTML differences |
145: | html | text | visible text | CSS, attributes, inline styles, scripts, layout |
146: | docx | text | paragraph and table text | formatting, styles, images, comments, tracked changes |
147: | pdf | text* | text layer only | layout, images; scanned/image-only PDFs (no OCR) |

149: `text*` (PDF) requires a local extractor — poppler's `pdftotext` or the `pypdf`/`pdfplumber` package. 150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 5. RULES
154: 
155: ### ✅ ALWAYS
156: 
157: - Capture the baseline **before** the edit; that ordering is an invariant.
158: - Keep everything local — no network, upload, or telemetry.
159: - State the format fidelity tier and any warnings honestly.
160: - Read a file before editing it; never modify the source document during comparison.
161: - Run `scripts/validate_report.py` on a generated report before handing it off, and report the result.
162: - Offer the explicit-pair fallback when no valid baseline exists.
163: - Require balanced, matching aggregate markers before presenting file-boundary chrome.
164: 
165: ### ⛔ NEVER
166: 
167: - Never mutate, overwrite, or "fix up" the source document — capture and comparison are read-only against it.
168: - Never present a `text`/`text*`-tier comparison as if it captured formatting, layout, or tracked changes.
169: - Never claim a diff was produced when the format was unsupported and no fallback ran.
170: - Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json` or `description.json`.
171: - Never send document content off-machine or fetch a remote resource into the report.
172: 
173: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
174: 
175: - When a PDF has no text layer (appears scanned) — the comparison would be empty; OCR is out of scope.
176: - When the document format is unsupported and no explicit pre-extracted pair can be provided.
177: - When the target document or output path is unknown and acting would be a guess.
178: 
179: ---
180:

184: 
185: 1. Confirm the source file is byte-for-byte unchanged (compare should never write to it).

187: 3. Report the change summary (`+added −removed ~changed`, possible moves, fidelity tier) and the report path.
188: 
189: If the validator fails, fix the renderer or report the failure explicitly — do not claim a clean, self-contained report.
190:

192:

194: 
195: The task is successful when:
196: 
197: - The correct workflow shape is used (automatic baseline when one exists; explicit pair otherwise), and code/Git/design/audit requests are deferred to their owners.
198: - The baseline was captured before the edit, or the explicit-pair fallback was used, and the source file is unchanged.
199: - A single self-contained, accessible HTML report is produced and passes `validate_report.py`.
200: - Valid aggregate pairs keep every file transition visible in both report views without leaking one file's Markdown section label into the next.
201: - The fidelity tier and any warnings are stated; a limited-fidelity result is never presented as complete.
202: - All processing stayed local, and no packet-local advisor metadata was created.
203:

52: A request to review what an AI or a person changed in a locally edited document, to capture a baseline before an edit or to compare two explicit versions selects this packet.
53: Two shapes exist: an automatic snapshot-backed baseline and an explicit pair.
54: The comparison reads extracted text only, so a visual or design comparison is out of scope.
55: 
56: `references/README.md` is the route map and the fallback load, and `references/cli-reference.md` holds the commands and exit codes.
57: 
58: A request that matches no registered mode returns `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK`, never a silent default.
59: 
60: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
65: 
66: All comparison, extraction, snapshotting, and rendering are done by `scripts/create_diff.py`. Run it from this packet directory (or give an absolute path to it). The invariant is: **capture the baseline before the edit** — a diff needs a real before-state.
67: 
68: ### Automatic flow (snapshot-backed)
69: 
70: ```bash
71: # 0. (optional) confirm what is supported and at what fidelity
72: python3 scripts/create_diff.py capabilities
73: 
74: # 1. BEFORE the edit — capture a baseline (copies the file into a local .create-diff/ store;
75: #    never touches the source)
76: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
77: 
78: # 2. ... let the edit happen (AI or human) ...
79: 
80: # 3. AFTER the edit — compare the current file against its latest baseline and render the report
81: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Explicit-pair flow (fallback — no stored state needed)
85: 
86: Use this when there is no baseline, when comparing two arbitrary versions, or when the automatic store is unavailable:
87: 
88: ```bash
89: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair --before old.md --after new.md --report review.html
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Pre-composed aggregate pairs
93: 
94: `compare-pair` can also review a pre-composed pair containing two or more files.
95: Wrap every file in both inputs with the same ordered, unique markers:
96: 
97: ```text
98: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/first.md =====
99: [file content]
100: ===== END FILE: docs/first.md =====
101: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/second.md =====
102: [file content]
103: ===== END FILE: docs/second.md =====
104: ```
105: 
106: When both inputs contain a balanced matching envelope, the report renders every
107: start and end as an explicit full-width boundary band. Boundaries stay visible
108: through collapsed context, later files receive a 32px canvas gap before their
109: start band, and transitions reset Markdown section labels between files. This
110: does not add native directory comparison or repeated multi-file CLI arguments;
111: callers compose the two aggregate documents before invoking `compare-pair`.
112: 
113: ### Report and verification
114: 
115: - The report is a single self-contained HTML file (inlined CSS, no scripts, no network). Views: `--view unified` (default) or `--view side-by-side`.
116: - Valid aggregate pairs display semantic `START FILE` and `END FILE` bands in both views; malformed envelopes remain ordinary document text.
117: - Without `--report`, the source stem is semantically normalized to lowercase kebab-case and emitted as `<source-slug>.diff.html`. An explicit report basename must already use lowercase kebab-case and the engine refuses to overwrite an existing report.
118: - Always verify a generated report is safe and self-contained before handing it off:
119: 
120: ```bash
121: python3 scripts/validate_report.py review.html
122: ```
123: 
124: ### Lifecycle helpers
125: 
126: ```bash
127: python3 scripts/create_diff.py status [path/to/doc.md]      # list stored baselines
128: python3 scripts/create_diff.py cleanup --older-than 14      # prune old baselines (add --dry-run to preview)
129: ```
130: 
131: ### Machine-readable output and exit codes
132: 
133: Add `--json` to `compare`, `compare-pair`, `capabilities`, or `status` for a structured summary. Exit codes: `0` success · `2` usage error · `3` unsupported/limited format with no fallback · `4` missing baseline snapshot · `5` I/O or extraction failure. Map these to actionable messages rather than swallowing them.
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 4. CAPABILITY & FIDELITY TIERS
138: 
139: State the tier to the user; never present a low-fidelity comparison as complete.
140: 
141: | Format | Tier | What is compared | Not compared |
142: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
143: | text | full | exact text | — |
144: | markdown | full | exact text + heading/section awareness | rendered-HTML differences |
145: | html | text | visible text | CSS, attributes, inline styles, scripts, layout |
146: | docx | text | paragraph and table text | formatting, styles, images, comments, tracked changes |
147: | pdf | text* | text layer only | layout, images; scanned/image-only PDFs (no OCR) |
148: 
149: `text*` (PDF) requires a local extractor — poppler's `pdftotext` or the `pypdf`/`pdfplumber` package. Run `capabilities` to see what is available; when none is, the engine says so and offers the explicit-pair fallback with pre-extracted text. Full detail: `references/capabilities-and-fidelity.md`.

151: ---
152: 
153: ## 5. RULES
154: 
155: ### ✅ ALWAYS
156: 
157: - Capture the baseline **before** the edit; that ordering is an invariant.
158: - Keep everything local — no network, upload, or telemetry.
159: - State the format fidelity tier and any warnings honestly.
160: - Read a file before editing it; never modify the source document during comparison.
161: - Run `scripts/validate_report.py` on a generated report before handing it off, and report the result.
162: - Offer the explicit-pair fallback when no valid baseline exists.
163: - Require balanced, matching aggregate markers before presenting file-boundary chrome.
164: 
165: ### ⛔ NEVER
166: 
167: - Never mutate, overwrite, or "fix up" the source document — capture and comparison are read-only against it.
168: - Never present a `text`/`text*`-tier comparison as if it captured formatting, layout, or tracked changes.
169: - Never claim a diff was produced when the format was unsupported and no fallback ran.
170: - Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json` or `description.json`.
171: - Never send document content off-machine or fetch a remote resource into the report.
172: 
173: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
174: 
175: - When a PDF has no text layer (appears scanned) — the comparison would be empty; OCR is out of scope.
176: - When the document format is unsupported and no explicit pre-extracted pair can be provided.
177: - When the target document or output path is unknown and acting would be a guess.
178: 
179: ---

182:

184: 
185: 1. Confirm the source file is byte-for-byte unchanged (compare should never write to it).

14: # Report accessibility & self-containment contract
15: 
16: Open this when a review asks what the generated HTML guarantees with scripting off, or before changing anything the validator checks.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: The report is meant to be reviewable by everyone, from `file://`, forever, with no dependencies. `scripts/validate_report.py` enforces the safety half of this; the guarantees below describe the whole contract.
23: 
24: ### When to Use
25: 
26: - Checking a report against the guarantees a reviewer exercises: scripting disabled, offline, keyboard-only or colour-blind.
27: - Confirming what `scripts/validate_report.py` enforces before trusting a `PASS`.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. SELF-CONTAINMENT (VALIDATED)
32: 
33: - Single HTML file. All CSS is inlined in one `<style>` block; there are no external stylesheets, fonts, scripts, or images.
34: - **Zero JavaScript.** No `<script>` tags and no inline event handlers (`onclick=`, etc.). The report is fully usable with scripting disabled.
35: - **No network.** No remote `href`/`src`. A restrictive Content-Security-Policy meta tag (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`) blocks any accidental request even if the file is opened in a browser.
36: - **Escaped content.** Every piece of source-document text is HTML-escaped, so a document containing markup (or a hostile `<script>`/`onerror=`) is shown as inert text, never executed.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 3. ACCESSIBILITY
41: 
42: - `<html lang="en">`, semantic landmarks (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>` with `aria-labelledby`), and a single `<h1>`.
43: - A "Skip to differences" link as the first focusable element.
44: - The change summary is a real `<table>` with row headers (`<th scope="row">`); the diff is a `<table>` with column headers.
45: - **Colour is never the only signal.** Added lines carry a `+`, removed lines a `−`, in a dedicated marker column with an `aria-label` ("added"/"removed"). Word-level changes use `<mark>` with a non-colour decoration in addition to the background tint — inline additions are underlined and inline removals are struck through — so the exact changed substring stays distinguishable for colour-blind users and in monochrome, not only in forced-colours mode.
46: - Contrast targets WCAG AA in both light and dark themes (`prefers-color-scheme`), using `color-scheme: light dark`.
47: - Relative units govern typography and content/column sizing so browser zoom and text scaling work (the 4px spacing scale, hairline borders, and radii use fixed pixel tokens).
48: - In the **unified** view, content wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) so the page itself never scrolls sideways.
49: - The **side-by-side** view keeps its two code columns aligned inside a scoped `overflow-x: auto` container that is given a `min-width`, so on a narrow viewport that diff region actually scrolls horizontally instead of collapsing the columns — while the surrounding page (header, summary, legend, footer) still reflows and never forces the whole document to scroll.
50: - That scroll container is keyboard-operable: it is a labelled `role="region"` with `tabindex="0"` and a visible focus ring, so a keyboard-only user can focus and scroll it.
51: - Long runs of unchanged lines are collapsed to a labelled "N unchanged lines" row to keep the report scannable.
52: - In validated aggregate reports, every file transition remains visible as a full-width table row group.
53: - `START FILE` is the strongest transition, `END FILE` explicitly closes the group, and both include the escaped path as visible text so color is never the only signal.
54: - Every file after the first receives a 32px canvas-colored spacer row marked `aria-hidden="true"`; that gap also masks the frame edges at its sides, so it reads as open whitespace without adding empty navigation to the accessibility tree.
55: - Boundary rows also reset Markdown section context, preventing a heading from one file from labelling changes in the next.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 4. VIEWS
60: 
61: - **Unified** (default): old/new line numbers, a marker column, and content in one column.
62: - **Side-by-side** (`--view side-by-side`): before and after in two columns, each with its own line numbers. The two-column grid is held in a scoped horizontal-scroll region so columns stay aligned rather than wrapping into each other on narrow viewports.
63: 
64: Both views share the same summary, fidelity notes, and legend.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 5. WHAT IS NOT GUARANTEED
69: 
70: The report reflects the extraction tier (see `capabilities-and-fidelity.md`). For `text`/`text*` formats it shows textual change only; it does not claim to show formatting, layout, or tracked-change fidelity, and says so in the "Fidelity notes" section.

33: ## 2. TIERS
34: 
35: | Tier | Meaning |
36: | --- | --- |
37: | `full` | Highest-fidelity text comparison — after the normalization described below (Unicode NFC, line endings, per-line trailing whitespace). |
38: | `text` | Visible/structural text only; formatting, styling, and non-text content are not compared. |
39: | `text*` | Text layer only, and only when an optional extractor is installed. |
40: | `unsupported` | No reliable local extraction available. |

43: ## 3. `snapshot`
44: 
45: Capture a baseline of a file into the local store (before an edit).
46: 
47: ```bash
48: python3 create_diff.py snapshot <file> [--state-dir DIR]
49: ```
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 4. `compare`
54: 
55: Compare a file against its latest baseline and render a report.
56: 
57: ```bash
58: python3 create_diff.py compare <file> \
59:   [--report OUT] [--view unified|side-by-side] [--state-dir DIR] [--json]
60: ```
61: 
62: Default report path: `<file-stem>.diff.html` in the current directory.
63: 
64: ---
65: 
66: ## 5. `compare-pair`
67: 
68: Compare two explicit files with no stored state.
69: 
70: ```bash
71: python3 create_diff.py compare-pair \
72:   --before A --after B \
73:   [--report OUT] [--view unified|side-by-side] \
74:   [--label-before L] [--label-after L] [--json]
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## 6. `status`
80: 
81: List stored baselines (all, or for one file).
82: 
83: ```bash
84: python3 create_diff.py status [<file>] [--state-dir DIR] [--json]
85: ```
86: 
87: ---
88: 
89: ## 7. `cleanup`
90: 
91: Remove stored baselines.
92: 
93: With no `--older-than`, all matching snapshots are removed. Use `--dry-run` to preview.
94: 
95: ```bash
96: python3 create_diff.py cleanup \
97:   [--file F] [--older-than DAYS] [--state-dir DIR] [--dry-run]
98: ```
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 8. FLAGS
103: 
104: | Flag | Applies to | Meaning |
105: | --- | --- | --- |
106: | `--report OUT` | compare, compare-pair | Output HTML path (default `<stem>.diff.html`). |
107: | `--view` | compare, compare-pair | `unified` (default) or `side-by-side`. |
108: | `--state-dir DIR` | snapshot, compare, status, cleanup | Snapshot store location (default `./.create-diff`). |
109: | `--json` | capabilities, compare, compare-pair, status | Emit a machine-readable summary instead of prose. |
110: | `--label-before/--label-after` | compare-pair | Names shown in the report. |
111: | `--older-than DAYS` | cleanup | Remove snapshots older than N days. |
112: | `--dry-run` | cleanup | Preview removals without deleting. |
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 9. EXIT CODES
117: 
118: | Code | Meaning |
119: | --- | --- |
120: | `0` | Success. |
121: | `2` | Usage error (bad arguments). |
122: | `3` | Unsupported/limited format with no fallback (e.g. PDF with no extractor). |
123: | `4` | Missing baseline snapshot for `compare`. |
124: | `5` | I/O or extraction failure. |
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 10. JSON SUMMARY SHAPE
129: 
130: `compare`/`compare-pair --json` prints:
131: 
132: ```json
133: {
134:   "format": "markdown",
135:   "fidelity_tier": "full",
136:   "added": 4, "removed": 0, "changed": 5,
137:   "unchanged": 12, "possible_moves": 0,
138:   "total_changes": 9, "identical": false,
139:   "report": "review.html"
140: }
141: ```
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 11. REPRODUCIBILITY
146: 
147: Set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to a fixed Unix timestamp to make report output byte-reproducible (the diff content is already deterministic; only the "Generated" timestamp varies otherwise).
148: 
149: ---
150: 
151: ## 12. REPORT VALIDATOR
152: 
153: ```bash
154: python3 validate_report.py <report.html> [more.html ...]
155: ```
156: 
157: Exits `0` if every report is safe/self-contained, `1` otherwise. Checks: doctype, `<html lang>`, a Content-Security-Policy meta tag, no `<script>` tags, no inline event handlers, and no remote `href`/`src` in real markup (escaped content is ignored).

12: ---
13: 
14: # Workflow: baseline, comparison, and lifecycle
15: 
16: Reach for this reference before a document changes, or when both versions are already in hand and the baseline is missing.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: Give every review a real before-state, so a change is judged against what the document actually said.
23: 
24: ### When to Use
25: 
26: - You control the moment before an edit and want the engine to hold the baseline.
27: - No baseline exists, or you are comparing two arbitrary versions.
28: - One review needs to cover multiple files.
29: - You need to inspect or prune stored baselines.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: The core invariant: **capture the baseline before the edit.** A before/after review needs a real before-state, and once a file is overwritten the original is gone. `create-diff` never mutates the source — capture copies it into a local store.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 2. AUTOMATIC FLOW (SNAPSHOT-BACKED)
38: 
39: Best when you control the moment before an edit (e.g. an AI is about to modify a document).
40: 
41: ```bash
42: # 1. BEFORE the edit
43: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
44: 
45: # 2. ... the edit happens ...
46: 
47: # 3. AFTER the edit
48: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
49: ```
50: 
51: `compare` uses the file's **latest** snapshot as the "before" and the current file as the "after". If no snapshot exists it exits `4` and tells you to snapshot first or use the explicit pair.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. EXPLICIT-PAIR FLOW (FALLBACK)
56: 
57: Best when there is no baseline, when comparing two arbitrary versions, or when the automatic store is unavailable or unwanted.
58: 
59: ```bash
60: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair \
61:   --before old.md --after new.md \
62:   --label-before "v1" --label-after "v2" \
63:   --report review.html
64: ```
65: 
66: No stored state is read or written. `--label-before`/`--label-after` set the names shown in the report (default: the file names).
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 4. PRE-COMPOSED AGGREGATE PAIRS
71: 
72: When one review needs to cover multiple files, compose one before document and
73: one after document with the same ordered, unique file markers:
74: 
75: ```text
76: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/first.md =====
77: [file content]
78: ===== END FILE: docs/first.md =====
79: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/second.md =====
80: [file content]
81: ===== END FILE: docs/second.md =====
82: ```
83: 
84: Run those aggregate documents through the ordinary `compare-pair` command. The
85: engine activates boundary mode only when both inputs contain at least two files
86: and every start/end pair is balanced, path-matched, unique, and in the same
87: order. Valid boundaries become explicit `START FILE` and `END FILE` bands in
88: both report views and cannot be hidden by collapsed context. Invalid envelopes
89: fall back to ordinary document text instead of producing partial file chrome.
90: 
91: This is a pre-composed input format, not native directory comparison or repeated
92: multi-file CLI arguments.
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 5. AFTER GENERATING A REPORT
97: 
98: Always validate the report before handing it off:
99: 
100: ```bash
101: python3 ../scripts/validate_report.py review.html
102: ```
103: 
104: Then report the change summary and the report path. If the source file changed during the run, something is wrong — comparison must be read-only against the source.
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: ## 6. WHERE SNAPSHOTS LIVE
109: 
110: Baselines are stored under a `.create-diff/` directory in the current working directory (override with `--state-dir DIR`).
111: 
112: - Each source path gets its own subdirectory, keyed by a hash of its absolute path.
113: - That subdirectory holds the copied blobs plus a `manifest.json` recording capture time, size, and SHA-256.
114: - Writes are atomic (temp file + rename).
115: - The source is only ever read.
116: 
117: Add `.create-diff/` to `.gitignore` if you run this inside a repository — it is local scratch state, not a deliverable.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 7. LIFECYCLE
122: 
123: ```bash
124: # What baselines exist (all, or for one file)
125: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py status
126: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py status path/to/doc.md
127: 
128: # Prune old baselines (preview first)
129: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py cleanup --older-than 14 --dry-run
130: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py cleanup --older-than 14
131: ```
132: 
133: `cleanup` with no `--older-than` removes all matching snapshots; scope it with `--file` and preview with `--dry-run`.

13: 
14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073: 
1074: ---
